newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean chip shares soar on hopes of recovery.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean chip shares soar on hopes of recovery.

text.p: Shares of South Korea's semiconductor companies soared in early afternoon trading on Thursday on expectations of a business recovery, brokers said.
Samsung Electronics, the world's leading memory chip maker, rose 3,400 won to 59,700. It briefly hit its daily upper-limit of 60,800.
On Wednesday U.S. research firm Dataquest reported that the worldwide dynamic random access memory (DRAM) market was showing signs of rebounding from last year's oversupply.
"I'm not sure why the reaction to chip maker stocks was delayed by a day, but the market's overall strength seems to be moving toward those stocks today," said Kim Heung-shik of Hyundai Securities.
LG Semicon was up 1,400 won to 21,000, while Hyundai Electronics went limit-up, climbing 2,000 won to 28,000.
Dataquest said the DRAM oversupply rate was likely to run at seven percent per quarter for most of 1997, down from the more than 10 percent oversupply in the first half of 1996.
